answer: Give every identity a kernel: a sequential proof-of-work bound to one hardware attestation key, costing about ten minutes of real compute per identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand proofs and a thousand keys. Newcomers join only through a vine: an established identity vouches for them and locks collateral that is slashed if the newcomer is caught sybilling. The public registry works like a lotus: each identity starts as a closed bud and blooms only after a full epoch with no successful challenge, so fakes stay visible and costly long before they can vote or earn.
